ai.summary: Marks up a keyboard shortcut as a real `<kbd>` element, styled as hard-edged chrome.
whenToUse: Documentation or a menu item names a key the reader should press
A shortcut appears inline with copy describing what it does
Several keys form one combination, such as Ctrl, Shift, and K
whenNotToUse: The keys are not actually pressable here — use Text; `<kbd>` promises input the reader can make
It is a button the user clicks with a keyboard shortcut beside it — the shortcut is a Kbd, the control is a Button
It is a code sample or a terminal command — that is a Code block, not input
ai.accessibility: Renders a real `<kbd>` in the light DOM rather than a styled `<span>`, so assistive technology can identify the text as key input instead of reading a bare word — the difference between 'Shift' the key and 'shift' the sentence. It takes no role and no tab stop: a shortcut is text, not a control. The monospace family is functional, not decorative — 'l', '1', and 'I' are the same glyph in most UI faces and a shortcut is copied by eye.
knownLimitations: There is no `variant` prop: this component has one look, and §4's two-prop rule applies to components with an axis to vary on
It renders the key combination as plain text; separating multiple keys with '+' is the consumer's choice, and the component adds no separator
